messages:
ana: FYI we're planning to prune a couple internal routing headers from the public SDKs next week to tidy the client surface. This is coming from platform; goal is less coupling with console internal metrics.

mike: which headers exactly? any examples?

ana: `X-RD-Route-Intent`, `X-RD-Internal-Meta`, and a tiny sampling header we added during the quota experiment.

rachel: tagging SDK owners @mike @sam — dropping `X-RD-Internal-Meta` will break some attribution glue the console does today. We rely on that for per-route sparkline mapping.

sam: can we not map using tokenized route id instead? the SDKs already emit `X-RD-RouteID` in most flows.

ana: platform prefers removing every header that was only for internal routers. `RouteID` is fine but it's not always present in older SDK versions — that was the main reason for the extra header.

mike: ok. if we remove them we'll need a graceful fallback in SDKs: prefer `RouteID`, fall back to parsing `Authorization` or emit an unmapped metric.

rachel: console team: fallback to unmapped metrics would inflate "unknown route" noise. Could we do a temporary shim: SDKs keep the header for N weeks but log a deprecation warning and include a sampling bit so console can filter?

sam: that seems reasonable. Implementation: py/ts/go SDKs add opt-in flag `preserveInternalHeaders` default true for 2 weeks, then switch to false during the rollout. We'll run canary in console to see delta.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: platform/prune-internal-headers -> canary at 2024-11-08T14:00Z

ana: plan sounds good. action items: (1) SDK owners add flag + warning, (2) console add sparkline filter for `unmapped`, (3) platform publish pruning RFC with exact header list. I'll author RFC.

mike: I'll open PR for py + ts + go with tests and an entry in CHANGELOG mentioning the temporary flag and the timeline :+1:

rachel: removing internal telemetry will help long term. thanks team — sync on standup if anything blocks.
